title: Dhanbad Coal Mining & Washeries: a note to the credit manager
narrative: Dhanbad sits on the Jharia coalfield, which [6] calls the only source of prime coking coal in the country — geographically monopolised supply, with 50+ small and medium cokeries and 30+ washery units around it [6]. **The business is easy to describe: buy raw coal at the minehead, pay to move it, wash or blend it to a grade a steel mill or thermal plant will accept, and sell the washed tonne.** Cash comes from the spread between raw coal plus washing plus freight, and the washed realisation. The local proof is narrow but real: BCCL's washeries earned ₹501.94 crore in the first half, 3.54 times higher, with washed coal production up 12.8% [4]. Be aware how thin city-level evidence is — [6] is an undated aggregator page, so its numbers are claims to verify, not facts to lend on.

**Working capital sits in the coal pile and the rent, not in the plant.** A first batch of 100–500 MT costs ₹30–50 lakh [6], and a rented 2000–3000 sqm washing unit runs ₹3–8 lakh a month [6]. A borrower who rents carries fixed monthly rent against a stock that a blockade can freeze in a day. [6] quotes 30–45% D2C gross margin and 15–25% wholesale margin; treat both as page claims. **So when a proposal lands, ask whether the washery is owned or rented and what the rent is; if the rent spread over the contracted monthly tonnage leaves nothing above the washing charge, ask for the signed offtake contract before you sanction.** Get the actual yield, the actual realisation and receivable days — collect from customer; no source here gives them.
## What has broken here this fortnight

**The risk in Dhanbad is not the coal price, it is the surface above the seam.** On 30 October, residents of Parghabad blocked Sudamdih ASP colliery's fire outsourced project over land compensation and pending purchases; production and coal transport stopped, and management promised approval by 7 November 2026 — the same date the Deputy Commissioner's land-purchase order expires [1]. On 29 October the same colliery was blocked over jobs and compensation, halting coal and overburden movement [2]. [1] records 15 years of pending claims, 2.16 acres used without payment and 3.88 acres under CNT case 21/24. **So when a proposal lands, ask which block the coal comes from; if that block has a live compensation or CNT case, cut tenor to the contract cycle and make a second source a condition of sanction.**
## What the peers are telling us

Peer results are mixed, and they are peer, not local. CIL's Q2FY27 production was 151 MT against a 158 MT target, offtake 186 MT, overburden 353 M.CuM against 374 M.CuM [5]; e-auction premium moderated to 51% from 57%, with ASP ₹1,647/t and e-auction realisation ₹2,283/t [5]. **Volumes are moving but auction-linked realisation is softening, so a trader or washery paid off e-auction parity is the one to underwrite hardest.** On the customer side, SAIL's imported coking coal reached ₹22,930/t, up ₹1,700 QoQ and a ₹3.2K swing against its own guidance, OPM at 12.9%, and FY27 volume guidance cut to 21 MT from 22 MT [3]; imported coal is 85% of its 19 MT basket [3]. **That is the real growth opening — domestic washed coking coal substituting an import at that landed price — but the umbrella price is set abroad, so your borrower's realisation moves without notice.**
## Who to pursue, who to avoid

**Pursue toll and beneficiation operators with a BCCL-linked supply and quality certification, and cokery feeders in the Jharia cluster — 50+ small and medium cokeries need backward integration [6].** [6] also describes traders who moved from ₹2–5 lakh to ₹50–100 lakh a month on long-term contracts; the page is undated and unverified, so lend to GST returns, not to the story. **Avoid first-time traders without mining or energy experience — [6] itself says the business is not for them, nor for anyone with under ₹20 lakh capital — and avoid any unit whose whole supply sits in one disputed block.**
**Unsecured room does exist: collateral-free lending to ₹20 lakh under RBI's MSME directions of 2026, and to ₹25 lakh on track record [6].** Build the discipline around what you take and when:
- Every month: washing invoice tally, diesel and freight bills, ROM-to-washed stock statement, e-way bills matched to GST.
- Every quarter: the supplier contract with its validity date, and the land case status at the Deputy Commissioner's office.
- Where none of this exists, collect from customer and hold the limit.
**Tie drawing power to the washing contract, not to spot e-auction; if the e-auction premium falls below the 51% recorded in [5], reprice the limit to FSA-linked cashflow.**
